p.src: Now Commander He was surnamed He and named Chongbao. He served as deputy commander under Chief Commander Wuyan of the Liao kingdom. He stood ten feet tall, possessed the strength to withstand ten thousand men, and was skilled in sorcery. He wielded a three-pointed, double-edged blade and, being stationed at Youzhou, now commanded the forces of every district. At that time He Chongbao memorialized the sovereign: “In the territory of Youzhou under your servant’s charge, there is a place called Greenstone Ravine. Only one road leads into it; lofty mountains surround it on every side, and there is no way out. I shall dispatch a dozen or so horsemen to lure this band of southern barbarians straight inside, then deploy our troops to surround them from without. With no road ahead and no retreat behind, the wretches will surely starve to death.” Chief Commander Wuyan said, “But how are we to entice the wretches there?” Commander He replied, “They have captured three of our great prefectures and are swollen with pride. They are certain to set their sights on Youzhou. We shall divide our forces here and send men to lure them on. They will certainly press their advantage and give chase. Once drawn into the mountain trap, where could they possibly flee?” Chief Commander Wuyan said, “I fear your scheme may not succeed, and that we shall still have to crush them with our main army. Nevertheless, let us see how you fare.”

p.src: Commander He then took leave of the sovereign, gathered his helmet, armor, blade, and horse, and returned to the city of Youzhou with his attendant foot soldiers. He mustered the troops and divided them into three divisions. One division was to hold Youzhou, while the other two advanced toward Bazhou and Jizhou. Having issued his orders, he sent the two divisions out of the city and appointed his two younger brothers to lead them. His elder brother He Chai was to attack Bazhou, and his younger brother He Yun to attack Jizhou. Neither was to win; they were merely to feign defeat and lure the enemy into the territory of Youzhou, where another stratagem awaited them. Meanwhile, as Song Jiang and the others held Bazhou, a messenger came to report: “The Liao forces have invaded Jizhou. For fear that it may be lost, we beg you to dispatch troops to its aid.” Song Jiang said, “Since they have come to attack, we must meet them in battle. Let us seize this opportunity to take Youzhou.” Song Jiang left a small force to hold Bazhou, while the rest of the great army struck camp and set out. He led the army to Jizhou, joined forces with Lu Junyi, and fixed a day for the advance.

p.src: Song Jiang joined Lu Junyi, and together they entered the command tent to discuss a plan for capturing Youzhou. Wu Yong and Zhu Wu said, “Youzhou has sent troops against us by two routes. This must be a scheme to lure us in, so we should not advance yet.” Lu Junyi said, “You strategists are mistaken! Those wretches have suffered defeat time and again. How could this be a scheme to lure us? If we fail to seize what lies within our grasp, it will be difficult to take later. If we do not march from here to capture Youzhou, what occasion are we waiting for?” Song Jiang said, “The wretches are at the end of their strength. What clever stratagem could they possibly employ? This is the perfect opportunity.” Thus, rejecting the advice of Wu Yong and Zhu Wu, he led the army straight toward Youzhou, dividing the combined forces from the two prefectures into three columns of differing size. p.src: The banner at the head of his army bore the clear inscription: “He Chongbao, Deputy Commander of the Great Liao.” He spurred his horse forward, leveled his blade, and emerged before the lines. Seeing him, Song Jiang said, “A commander of the Liao kingdom must be a mighty general. Who dares ride out against him?” Before he had finished speaking, Guan Sheng the Great Blade flourished his Green Dragon Crescent Blade, urged on his Red Hare horse, and flew from the ranks. Without exchanging a word, he engaged Commander He. After more than thirty bouts, Commander He could no longer sustain his strength. He turned aside Guan Sheng’s blade, wheeled around, and fled toward his own lines. Guan Sheng galloped in pursuit, while Commander He led his defeated troops around the hillside. Song Jiang then ordered the army to pursue. After they had gone some forty or fifty li, battle drums suddenly thundered on every side. Just as Song Jiang urgently ordered the troops to turn back, a body of Liao soldiers came charging from the left of the hillside and blocked their way. As Song Jiang hastily divided his forces to meet them, another Liao contingent came charging from the right. Ahead, Commander He reined in his troops, turned back, and joined the attack. Song Jiang’s troops could not respond quickly enough on every side, and the Liao army smashed their formation into two.

p.src: Meanwhile, as Lu Junyi fought with the troops in the rear, he lost sight of the army ahead. He urgently sought a way through, intending to fight his way back, when another Liao force burst from a hollow beside the road and engaged him. The Liao troops raised battle cries that shook the heavens and charged from every side, surrounding them on both left and right in the heart of the encirclement. Lu Junyi deployed his generals, charging left and right and sweeping back and forth through the enemy as they sought a road of escape. The generals displayed their valor, summoned all their spirit, and were rushing in every direction to do battle when suddenly dark clouds closed overhead and black mist blotted out the sky. Day became like night, and east, west, north, and south could no longer be distinguished. Alarmed, Lu Junyi hastily gathered a body of troops and fought desperately to break out. In the darkness he heard the jingling of bridle bells ahead, so he spurred his horse and led his soldiers toward the sound, fighting as they went. When they reached a mountain pass, they heard voices and neighing horses within. He led the army in pursuit, but as they entered, a furious wind sprang up, hurling stones and driving sand so thickly that nothing could be seen even face-to-face. Lu Junyi fought his way deep inside. It was around the second watch before the wind finally subsided and the clouds parted, revealing a sky full of stars once more. When they looked around, they saw lofty mountains on every side, with sheer cliffs to left and right. There were only steep peaks and rugged ridges, with no path by which they might climb out. Of all the horse and foot who had followed him, there remained only the twelve leaders Xu Ning, Suo Chao, Han Tao, Peng Qi, Chen Da, Yang Chun, Zhou Tong, Li Zhong, Zou Yuan, Zou Run, Yang Lin, and Bai Sheng, together with five thousand troops. By starlight they tried to find the road back, but high mountains enclosed them on every side, and there was no way out. Lu Junyi said, “The soldiers have fought all day and are weary in body and spirit. Let us rest here for the night and give the warhorses a respite. Tomorrow we shall search again for the road back.”

p.src: Meanwhile, as Song Jiang was fighting, black clouds suddenly rose on every side, stones rolled and sand flew, and the soldiers could no longer see those facing them. But Gongsun Sheng, who was riding with the army, saw this and knew it to be sorcery. He hastily drew his precious sword and performed his art on horseback, muttering an incantation before shouting, “Begone!” Wherever he pointed the precious sword, the dark clouds scattered and the wild wind abruptly ceased; the Liao army retreated without further fighting. Song Jiang drove his troops through the encirclement, withdrew to a high mountain, and rejoined the forces under his command. For the time being, he linked the provision carts end to end and used them as a stockade. When the leaders great and small were mustered, Lu Junyi and twelve others were missing, together with more than five thousand troops and horses. At daybreak, Song Jiang sent Huyan Zhuo, Lin Chong, Qin Ming, and Guan Sheng, each with a body of troops, to search in every direction. They searched all day but returned without the least news. Song Jiang then took out the Mystic Maiden’s divination text, burned incense, and cast an oracle. When he had finished, he said, “The principal sign gives no cause for alarm, but they are trapped in a dark and hidden place and will not easily escape soon.” Still unable to set his mind at ease, Song Jiang sent Xie Zhen and Xie Bao disguised as hunters to search around the mountain. He also dispatched Shi Qian, Shi Yong, Duan Jingzhu, and Cao Zheng to seek information in every direction.

p.src: Now Xie Zhen and Xie Bao put on tiger-skin coats, shouldered their steel forks, and headed deep into the mountains. As evening drew near, the two reached the mountains and looked all around. There was no sign of habitation, only range upon range of rugged peaks. Xie Zhen and Xie Bao crossed several more ridges. That night the moonlight was hazy, and far away they saw a single lamp gleaming by the mountainside. The brothers said, “Where there is lamplight, there must be a household. Let us go there and ask for something to eat.” Fixing their eyes on the light, they lengthened their stride and hurried toward it. After going little more than a li, they came to a place beside a wooded slope. There stood two or three thatched huts, with lamplight shining through a broken wall beneath the eaves. Xie Zhen and Xie Bao pushed open the wooden door and saw by the lamplight an old woman over sixty years of age. The brothers set down their steel forks and bowed their heads to the floor. The old woman said, “I thought it was my sons coming home, but instead it is travelers who have arrived. Travelers, there is no need to bow. Where are you hunters from? How did you come here?” Xie Zhen said, “We are natives of Shandong and were born into a family of hunters. We came here to conduct some trade, but unfortunately found ourselves amid armies in turmoil and battle after battle. Thus we lost our capital and have no means of livelihood. We brothers therefore had no choice but to enter the mountains and seek some game to sustain ourselves. But we did not know the paths and lost our way, and so arrived here to ask shelter in your home for one night. We beg you, grandmother, to take us in!” The old woman said, “As the old saying goes, ‘Who travels with his house upon his head?’ My two sons are hunters too, and they should be home presently! Sit awhile, travelers. I shall prepare some supper for you both.” Xie Zhen and Xie Bao thanked her, saying, “We are deeply grateful, grandmother!” The old woman went into the inner room. The brothers sat down before the door. Before long, two men appeared outside, carrying a roe deer between them. As they entered, they called, “Mother, where are you?” The old woman came out and said, “My sons, you are home. Put down the deer and come meet these two travelers.” Xie Zhen and Xie Bao hurriedly bowed low. After the two men returned the courtesy, they asked, “Where are you travelers from? What brings you here?” Xie Zhen and Xie Bao repeated what they had just told the old woman. The two men said, “Our family has lived here for generations. I am Liu Er, and my younger brother is Liu San. Our father, Liu Yi, unfortunately died, leaving only our mother. We live solely by hunting and have done so here for twenty or thirty years. The paths here are extremely tangled, and even we do not know some places. Since you two are from Shandong, how could you possibly find food and clothing here? Do not deceive us. Surely you two are not really hunters?” Xie Zhen and Xie Bao said, “Now that we have come here, how could we conceal it? We shall tell you the truth, elder brothers.” A poem bears witness:

p.src: At once Xie Zhen and Xie Bao knelt on the ground and said, “We truly are hunters from Shandong. We brothers are called Xie Zhen and Xie Bao. We followed our elder brother Song Gongming as outlaws at Liangshan Marsh for many years. Now that we have accepted amnesty, we have accompanied him here to defeat the Liao realm. The other day, during a great battle with Commander He, his charge scattered us. One division of our army has vanished, and we do not know where it is trapped, so we brothers were specially sent to gather information.” The two brothers laughed and said, “Since you two are men of valor, please rise. We shall show you the way. Sit awhile. We shall cook a haunch of roe deer, warm a cup of our village wine, and set out a meal for you both.” Before a single watch had passed, the meat was cooked and brought out. Liu Er and Liu San entertained Xie Zhen and Xie Bao. As they drank, the brothers asked, “We have long heard that Song Gongming of your Liangshan Marsh carries out Heaven’s justice and does no harm to innocent people. The report has spread even to our Liao realm.” Xie Zhen and Xie Bao replied, “Our elder brother holds loyalty and righteousness above all. He has sworn never to disturb or harm the good, but to kill only corrupt officials and cruel functionaries, and those who rely on strength to oppress the weak.” The two men said, “We had only heard the stories, but now we know they are true!” All were delighted and grew so fond of one another that they were reluctant to part. Xie Zhen and Xie Bao said, “That division of ours has more than ten leaders and three to five thousand soldiers, yet we have no idea where they have gone. I imagine it would take a large tract of ground to entrap them.” The two men said, “You do not know the terrain of our northern country. Here, within the jurisdiction of Youzhou, there is a place called Greenstone Ravine. Only one road leads in, while on all four sides rise lofty mountains of sheer cliffs and precipitous valleys. If that entrance road is blocked, no one can ever come out again. They are most likely trapped there. There is no other spacious place of that kind hereabouts. The place where your Vanguard Song is now encamped is called Mount Dulu. The level ground before that mountain is suitable for battle. From the summit, one can see troops approaching from every direction. If you wish to rescue that division, you must risk your lives to force open Greenstone Ravine; only then can you bring them out. There must be many troops at the mouth of Greenstone Ravine, cutting off the entrance. Cypresses grow thickly on this mountain, but at the mouth of Greenstone Ravine stand two great cypresses, the largest of all, shaped like spreading parasols and visible from every side. The ravine entrance lies right beside those great trees. There is one more thing against which you must guard: Commander He can work sorcery. Tell Vanguard Song to break his spells; that is vital.”

There is no other spacious place of that kind hereabouts.
The place where your Vanguard Song is now encamped is called Mount Dulu.
The level ground before that mountain is suitable for battle.
From the summit, one can see troops approaching from every direction.
If you wish to rescue that division, you must risk your lives to force open Greenstone Ravine; only then can you bring them out.
There must be many troops at the mouth of Greenstone Ravine, cutting off the entrance.
Cypresses grow thickly on this mountain, but at the mouth of Greenstone Ravine stand two great cypresses, the largest of all, shaped like spreading parasols and visible from every side.
The ravine entrance lies right beside those great trees.
There is one more thing against which you must guard: Commander He can work sorcery. Tell Vanguard Song to break his spells; that is vital.”

p.src: Having learned this, Xie Zhen and Xie Bao thanked the two Liu brothers and returned to the stronghold that very night. When Song Jiang saw them, he asked, “Did you two discover anything definite?” Xie Zhen and She Bao then recounted in full what the Liu brothers had told them. Song Jiang was startled and at once summoned the strategist Wu Yong to confer. While they were speaking, a junior officer came to report, “Duan Jingzhu and Shi Yong have brought Bai Sheng here.” Song Jiang said, “Bai Sheng was trapped together with Vanguard Lu. There must be some extraordinary reason for his coming.” They were immediately summoned before the command tent and questioned. Duan Jingzhu spoke first: “Shi Yong and I were keeping watch beside a mountain ravine when we saw a great felt bundle come rolling down from the summit. As we watched, it rolled almost to the foot of the mountain. It proved to be a bundle of felt garments, wrapped tight on every side and securely bound with rope. When we went over to the trees to examine it, we found Bai Sheng inside.”

p.src: Bai Sheng then said, “Chief Lu, I, and the other twelve men were in the midst of battle when suddenly heaven and earth grew dark, the sun lost its light, and we could no longer tell east from west or north from south. We could hear nothing but men shouting and horses neighing, and Chief Lu ordered us simply to keep fighting our way forward. Who could have imagined that we were plunging deep into the enemy’s most perilous ground? We found ourselves surrounded by lofty mountains on every side, with no way out and no provisions or fodder reaching us. Our whole company of men and horses was in desperate straits. Chief Lu ordered me to roll down from the mountaintop, find a way through, and carry word back. By good fortune, I ran straight into Shi Yong and Duan Jingzhu. Please send rescuing troops at once, Elder Brother, to go to their aid. If you delay, our commanders will surely perish.”

p.src: When Song Jiang had heard him out, he mustered his troops that very night and ordered Xie Zhen and Xie Bao to lead the way. They were to head for the great cypress trees, which marked the mouth of the valley. He passed down orders for horse and foot to combine their strength, fight their way forward, and open the valley mouth at all costs. The men and horses marched until dawn, when in the distance they saw two great cypresses before the mountain, shaped indeed like the canopies of parasols. Xie Zhen and Xie Bao immediately led the troops in an assault upon the mountain front. At the valley mouth, Commander He drew up his troops, and his two brothers vied with each other to ride out and meet the enemy. Song Jiang’s officers and men surged forward together to seize the valley mouth. Lin Chong, the “Panther Head,” galloped ahead and met He Chai. They had crossed weapons for only two bouts when Lin Chong thrust his spear into He Chai’s belly and knocked him from his horse. When the infantry chiefs saw that the cavalry had arrived first and won the advantage, they rushed in all the more fiercely. Li Kui, the “Black Whirlwind,” whirled his twin axes and hacked down Liao soldiers all along his path. Close behind came Fan Rui, the “Demon King of Chaos,” and Bao Xu, the “God of Death,” leading the shield-bearers Xiang Chong and Li Gun and a great body of men with barbarian shields, straight into the ranks of the Liao army. Li Kui met He Yun head-on, dashed beneath his horse, and severed one of its legs with a blow of his axe. The horse instantly collapsed, throwing He Yun from the saddle. Li Kui’s twin axes flew as he chopped wildly at both man and horse without pause. The Liao troops were pressing forward when they collided on both flanks with the shield-bearers under Fan Rui and Bao Xu. When Commander He saw that he had lost both brothers, he began muttering incantations and working sorcery of some unknown kind. Suddenly a furious wind arose and clouds welled up from the earth, shrouding the mountaintop in blackness and plunging the valley mouth into a gloomy murk. While the spell was taking effect, Gongsun Sheng rode out from the Song ranks. He drew his precious sword in the saddle, murmured no more than a few phrases, then shouted, “Haste!” At once wild winds swept in from every side, scattering the floating clouds and revealing a brilliant red sun. The commanders of all three divisions, horse and foot alike, drove forward and fought the Liao soldiers with utter disregard for death. Seeing that his magic had failed and the enemy was pressing the attack fiercely, Commander He brandished his saber, spurred his horse, and charged across the battle line. The two armies became locked in a general melee, and the Song troops drove the Liao soldiers fleeing in every direction.

p.src: The cavalry pursued the fleeing Liao troops, while the infantry set about clearing the valley mouth. It turned out that the Liao soldiers had blocked the exit by piling it layer upon layer with great slabs of blue stone. The infantry cleared the valley mouth and fought their way into Greenstone Valley. When Lu Junyi saw Song Jiang’s troops, he and his companions all expressed their shame. Song Jiang gave orders to cease the pursuit of the Liao troops for the time being, withdraw to Dulu Mountain, and let the rescued men and horses recover. When Lu Junyi saw Song Jiang, he burst into loud sobs and said, “Had you not graciously come to our rescue, dear brother, I would nearly have lost my life!” Song Jiang and Lu Junyi rode back to the stronghold alongside Wu Yong and Gongsun Sheng. There they rested the three armies, removed their armor, and took a brief respite.

p.src: The next day, Strategist Wu said, “We should take advantage of this opportunity to capture Youzhou. Once Youzhou is ours, the fall of the Liao realm will be close at hand.” Song Jiang ordered Lu Junyi and the other thirteen men, together with their troops, to return to Jizhou and rest there for the time being. He himself led all his commanders and soldiers away from Dulu Mountain and advanced to attack Youzhou.

p.src: Commander He had just retreated into the city and was greatly troubled by the loss of his two brothers. Then he heard a scout report, “Song Jiang’s army is coming to attack Youzhou.” The Liao troops grew even more alarmed. The Liao soldiers climbed the walls to look out and saw a mass of red banners to the northeast and a mass of blue banners to the northwest, two bodies of troops racing toward Youzhou. They immediately reported this to Commander He. Commander He was greatly startled by the news, but when he personally climbed the wall and looked, he recognized the banners as those of Liao and was overjoyed. The red-bannered force bore silver lettering on every standard. It was the army of Xu Qing, Prince Consort Taizhen of the Great Liao, and numbered only a little over five thousand men. The blue-bannered force had standards inscribed in gold and adorned throughout with pheasant feathers. It belonged to the great general Li Jinwu. This foreign officer held the posts of Palace Attendant, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Senior General of the Left Jinwu Guard. His surname was Li and his given name Ji, though he was known as Li Jinwu. A descendant of Li Ling, he had inherited the Jinwu title through his family’s privilege. He was then stationed at Xiongzhou with some ten thousand troops under his command. These were the very men who had been raiding the borders of the Great Song. On hearing that the Liao sovereign had lost several cities, they had therefore been ordered to bring their troops and assist in the fighting. When Commander He saw them, he sent men to tell both armies not to enter the city, but to conceal themselves behind the mountains and rest for the moment. When his own troops marched out and Song Jiang’s army approached, they were to fall upon it from left and right. Having sent these instructions, Commander He led his troops out of Youzhou to meet the enemy.

p.src: Song Jiang and his commanders had already drawn near Youzhou. Wu Yong said, “If they shut the gates and refuse to come out, they will have made no special preparations. But if they lead their troops out of the city to meet us, they must have an ambush laid. We should first divide our army into three columns before advancing. One column will advance directly toward Youzhou and engage the approaching enemy. The other two will serve like wings, guarding the left and right flanks. If an ambushing force rises, those two columns can be sent against it.” Song Jiang accordingly assigned Guan Sheng, with Xuan Zan and Hao Siwen, to command the left, and Huyan Zhuo, with Shan Tinggui and Wei Dingguo, to command the right. Each force numbered over ten thousand men and proceeded slowly along narrow paths behind the mountains. Song Jiang and the others led the main army forward, advancing directly toward Youzhou.

p.src: Now Commander He led his troops forward and came face-to-face with Song Jiang's army. The two armies confronted each other. Lin Chong rode out and engaged Commander He, but before they had exchanged five bouts, Commander He wheeled his horse and fled. Song Jiang's forces gave chase. Commander He divided his troops into two columns and, rather than entering Youzhou, skirted the city and fled. From horseback, Wu Yong called out, “Do not pursue them!” Before he had finished speaking, Imperial Son-in-law Taizhen charged out from the left, only to find Guan Sheng there to meet him. Li Jinwu charged out from the right and was likewise met by Huyan Zhuo. The three columns of troops now converged and pressed the enemy into a great battle; corpses covered the fields, and blood flowed in rivers.

p.src: Commander He realized that the Liao army could not prevail. As he tried to return to Youzhou, he ran into two generals who intercepted and attacked him: Hua Rong and Qin Ming, who held him fast in a desperate fight. Commander He tried to retreat toward the western gate, but then encountered Dong Ping, the “General of the Twin Spears,” and fought another bout with him; turning past the southern gate, he encountered Zhu Tong and fought yet another bout; Commander He dared not enter the city. Finding a broad road, he fled northward. But before he knew it, he came upon Huang Xin, the “Guardian of the Three Mountains,” who brandished his great saber and charged straight at him. Commander He panicked and was caught unprepared; Huang Xin brought his saber down squarely upon his horse's head. Commander He abandoned his horse and fled on foot, but unexpectedly Yang Xiong and Shi Xiu, two infantry leaders, sprang from a concealed hollow beside him. Together they seized him and threw him face down beneath them. Song Wan came charging after them with his spear leveled. Fearing that a quarrel over credit might damage their brotherhood, the men all thrust their spears into Commander He and killed him on the spot. That contingent of Liao soldiers had already scattered, each fleeing for his life. Imperial Son-in-law Taizhen saw the commander's banner fall amid the commander's ranks and the soldiers scatter. Realizing that all was lost, he led his column of red-banner troops away behind the mountain. In the midst of battle, Li Jinwu noticed that the red-banner troops had disappeared. Judging that the situation was hopeless, he too led his column of blue-banner troops in retreat behind the mountain.

p.src: When Song Jiang saw all three enemy columns retreat, he drove his army forward in force to seize Youzhou. Without commotion or alarm, they took it at the first beat of the drum. After entering Youzhou, he stationed the three armies there and at once issued proclamations to reassure the people. He immediately dispatched men to Tanzhou with an urgent report of victory, asking Privy Councillor Zhao to move his troops to Jizhou and defend it, and to bring the naval commanders and their vessels to Youzhou to await orders; meanwhile, he instructed Deputy Vanguard Lu Junyi to divide his forces and guard Bazhou. Altogether, they had now taken four great prefectures. Pacification Commissioner Zhao was delighted upon receiving the dispatch. On the one hand, he submitted a memorial to the court; on the other, he sent official orders to Jizhou and Bazhou, informing them that the naval commanders were to be dispatched again, make ready, and advance, in preparation for a combined assault by land and water.

p.src: Meanwhile, the ruler of Liao ascended the throne hall and assembled his civil and military officials. The Left Chancellor Youxi Bojin, the Right Chancellor and Grand Preceptor Chu Jian, the commanding generals, and the other officials deliberated before the throne: “At present, Song Jiang is invading our borders and has occupied four of our great prefectures. Sooner or later he will surely attack the imperial capital, and Yanjing will be difficult to defend. Commander He and his two brothers are already dead. At this time of national crisis, how do you, my civil and military ministers, propose that we deal with the matter?” Then Supreme Commander Wuyan Guang memorialized, “Your Majesty, do not be troubled! Many times before, your servant asked only to lead the army in person, but each time others obstructed me. Thus the rebels were allowed to grow strong, bringing about this great disaster. I humbly beg Your Majesty to issue a personal decree authorizing me to select and deploy the troops, unite the forces from every quarter, and raise an army on an appointed day. I shall make it my duty to capture Song Jiang and his followers and recover the cities they have taken.” The ruler approved his request and bestowed upon Commander Wuyan the pearl-studded tiger tally, the golden seal and imperial edict, the yellow battle-axe and white yak-tail standard, and the vermilion banners and black canopy, entrusting them all to him. “Whether members of the imperial line, relatives of the royal house, or troops of any kind whatsoever, all shall obey your command. Raise the army at once and march out to conquer the enemy!”

p.src: Having received the imperial decree and military tally, Commander Wuyan went down to the drill ground, assembled the many Liao generals, issued his commands, and ordered troops from every quarter to come and support the campaign. Just as he finished issuing his orders, his eldest son, Wuyan Yanshou, came straight to the military pavilion and reported: “Father, while you muster and inspect the main army, let me take several valiant generals ahead, join the forces of Imperial Son-in-law Taizhen and General Li Jinwu, and reach Youzhou first. We shall smash those southerners until scarcely a fifth of their strength remains. When you arrive, Father, we can catch them like a turtle in a jar and sweep Song's army away at a single drumbeat. May I ask what you think of this proposal?” Commander Wuyan said, “My son, your proposal is sound. I give you five thousand shock cavalry and twenty thousand elite troops. You shall serve as vanguard, join forces at once with Imperial Son-in-law Taizhen and General Li Jinwu, and depart immediately. As soon as you win a victory, send an urgent dispatch by swift courier.” The young general gladly accepted his orders, mustered the entire force, and marched straight toward Youzhou. Indeed, ten thousand galloping horses made heaven and earth tremble, and a thousand ranks surging forward struck fear into ghosts and gods. How the young General Wuyan challenged the enemy to battle will be told in the next chapter.
